concerns.text: Task T014a (Create cleaned_dataset.csv) is marked as depending on T013b (Validate MMSE column). However, T013b is marked `[ ]` (incomplete) and T014a is marked `[X]` (complete). This creates a semantic ordering violation where a consumer task is marked complete before its producer (the MMSE flag logic) exists. T014a cannot logically depend on a non-existent flag for downstream filtering logic.

Task T014b (Calculate validity metrics) depends on T012 (Exclusion logic). T012 is marked `[X]` (complete) but T014b is marked `[ ]` (incomplete). While the dependency direction is correct, the 'Independent Test' for US1 requires verifying the output contains a dataframe with valid records. If T014b is incomplete, the specific metric 'percentage of valid records' (SC-001) cannot be generated, breaking the independent testability of US1 as a shippable unit.

Task T027 (Robustness check using MMSE) depends on T013b (MMSE flag). T013b is `[ ]` (incomplete) and T027 is `[~]` (deferred). The dependency chain is broken: T027 cannot execute the 'If has_mmse=True' logic if T013b never sets the flag. This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' rule for the MMSE validation artifact.

Task T036c (Generate paper/001_results.md) depends on T036b and T036d. T036d (Fetch metadata for stimuli validation) is marked `[ ]` (incomplete). The final report generation (T036c) cannot include the 'scientific validity status' (SC-006) if the verification task (T036d) is not executed. This breaks the end-to-end testability of the final deliverable.

Task T015 (Stimulus file integrity check) is marked `[ ]` (incomplete) but is listed as a dependency for the 'Independent Test' of US1 which requires 'matching stimulus IDs'. The test cannot be fully validated if the integrity check logic is missing. Re-order or mark T015 as `[X]` if the logic is assumed to be in T010.
